title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's 'linearized' study of the loop equations (équation des lacets). Here the profinite group Π̂_{0,3} = π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) is replaced by its image in GL(2,Ẑ). That image comes through the identification P^1−{0,1,∞} ≅ H/Γ(2), in which Π_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2)/±1. The loop around 0 maps to l_0, with l_0^n = [[1,−2n],[0,1]]; the page's formulas a−2nc, b−2nd confirm this form of l_0.

The unknowns are pairs (α_0, f). Here α_0 = [[a,b],[c,d]] lies in GL(2,Ẑ) with det α_0 = ±1, and f = [[r,s],[t,u]] lies in SL(2,Ẑ). They satisfy equations (48), (49), (56), summarised as (93): α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1} = ε l_0^ν (f σ_∞(f)^{-1}), with ε = ±1. Here ρ and σ_∞ are the relevant involutions or automorphisms, and ν is presumably tied to the cyclotomic exponent.

The Remark observes that the additive group Ẑ acts on the solution set by left multiplication by powers of l_0: (α_0, f) ↦ (l_0^n α_0, l_0^n f). This action changes only the top rows, (a,b) ↦ (a−2nc, b−2nd) and (r,s) ↦ (r−2nt, s−2nu). The bottom rows (c,d) and (t,u) are unchanged: they are invariants of the coset Γ_∞\GL_2, i.e. of the stabiliser of the cusp ∞. Up to the factor 2, this action is exactly the indeterminacy of the solutions once c, d, t, u are fixed, as established in (87) and the accompanying proposition. The factor 2 only ensures that the congruence normalisation α'_0 ≡ f' ≡ id (mod 2) is preserved.

Grothendieck therefore concludes that what is intrinsically determined, outside the induced action of Π̂_{0,3} commuting with σ_∞, is essentially two things:
(a) a scalar μ ∈ Ẑ^* (the cyclotomic-type multiplier), which determines the signs ε_2(μ) and ε_3(μ);
(b) four quantities c, d, t, u ∈ Ẑ, subject to the 'sempiternal' relation (86): ε_2(t^2+u^2) = ε_2(c^2+cd+d^2) = 1/μ, and the parity conditions c ≡ t ≡ 0 and d ≡ u ≡ 1 (mod 2).

The two quadratic forms are the norm forms of Z[i] and Z[ω]. They reflect the elliptic points of order 2 and 3 of the modular group. Under the parity conditions t^2+u^2 ≡ 1 (mod 4), which is why a sign ε_2 is needed in order to reach every unit μ^{-1}. This matches the previous page's ε_2 ε_3 ≡ 1+c (mod 4).

Finally, Grothendieck notes that §91 (24bis) gave a natural normalisation inside Π̂_{0,3} that would remove the l_0^n ambiguity of f. He judges it instructive to ignore that normalisation for now, so as to highlight the crucial role of c, d, t, u (continued on the next page). The purpose is to parametrise the GL_2/SL_2 shadow of solutions of the loop equations, i.e. of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type data, by arithmetic invariants.
errors: No genuine mathematical error is visible. The action l_0^n is computed correctly given l_0 = [[1,−2],[0,1]]. One small point: the solution set is a torsor under Ẑ acting via 2n only 'up to the factor 2', so the l_0-orbit is of index ≤ 2 in the fibre over fixed (c,d,t,u). This matches the Z/2-torsor 'mystère' on the previous page, which is not resolved here.
Writing ε_2 = ε_2(μ), ε_3 = ε_3(μ) presupposes that the signs are functions of μ alone. That is consistent with (90), but it is not reproved here.

ideas.what: Ẑ acts on solutions of the linearized loop equations by left multiplication with powers of the cusp-stabilising unipotent l_0; fixing the bottom rows (c,d), (t,u) gives a torsor (up to index 2)
ideas.modern_name: action of the cusp stabiliser Γ_∞ ∩ Γ(2) on cosets; bottom row as invariant of Γ_∞\SL_2

ideas.what: Intrinsic invariants of a solution: μ ∈ Ẑ^* and (c,d,t,u) with ε_2(t^2+u^2) = ε_2(c^2+cd+d^2) = 1/μ and parity conditions
ideas.modern_name: representation of the inverse cyclotomic character by the norm forms of Z[i] and Z[ω] (elliptic points of order 2 and 3) in the SL_2(Ẑ)-shadow of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; GT's action on SL_2(Ẑ) / B_3 quotients was studied by Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, but this explicit quadratic-form parametrisation is not standard

ideas.what: Natural normalisation of f inside Π̂_{0,3} removing the l_0^n ambiguity (referred back to §91 (24bis))
ideas.modern_name: normalisation of GT elements, e.g. f in the commutator subgroup / the condition fixing the 'f' of (λ,f)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses GT-type equations only loosely

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates (c,d,t,u) with the twin quadratic-form condition as the 'crucial' invariants of the linearized loop equations. He deliberately postpones the normalisation of f and leaves the Z/2-torsor ambiguity as a 'mystère'. A systematic study of the linear (GL_2(Ẑ)) shadow of the GT equations, phrased through the Gaussian and Eisenstein norm forms, does not seem to be a standard part of the GT literature.
missed.quote: satisfaisant la sempiternelle relation (86) ε_2(t^2+u^2) = ε_2(c^2+cd+d^2) = 1/μ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an explicit arithmetic description of the image of GT/Galois-type solutions in GL_2(Ẑ), linking elliptic points of the modular group to the cyclotomic character. This could serve as a concrete test case for understanding the image of GT in the congruence completion.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful bookkeeping remark about an ambiguity, l_0^n acting on bottom-row-fixed solutions, plus an identification of intrinsic invariants. The quadratic-form relation is mildly interesting but was already introduced earlier as (86). The mathematics is elementary once the setting is known.
transcription_corrections: The label '(93bis)' should be read '(94)'; the image shows (93), (94), (95), (96), (97) in sequence.
'[-Un-] facteur 2 près' should be 'À un facteur 2 près dans 2n, c'est justement l'indétermination ...'
The interlinear insertion reads roughly 'Le facteur 2 ici assure seulement que les nouvelles solutions satisfont encore α'_0 ≡ f'_0 ≡ id (2)'.
'c'est en plus un moins que' should probably be 'c'est, plus ou moins, que'.
The final words 'il me semble intrinsèquement' should be 'il me semble instructif', continuing onto the next page as '... instructif pour le moment d'ignorer cette possibilité de normalisation'.
'j'y {+reviendrai+} [-peut-être-]' : the image suggests 'j'y reviendrai peut-être aussi par la suite'.
